content.jointProblem: Can a per-site, unsupervised baseline detector calibrated on unlabelled Modbus and BACnet/IP traffic detect behaviour drift in ArmaturaSec's ProtoSense deployments with low false alarms and plain-language explanations, with transfer to BACnet/IP and embedded hardware tested in the first experiment?

rationale.text: Kiss's group works directly on unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for ICS protocol traffic using statistical baseline modelling.

sources.quote: unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for industrial control system protocol traffic, using statistical baseline modelling

rationale.text: She has built per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP and evaluated a one-class detector at a 0.5% false positive rate on a live substation testbed.

sources.quote: per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed
At a false positive rate of 0.5%, the detector achieved a true positive rate of 91.4% across all attack types.

rationale.text: She has methods for threshold calibration when labelled attack data are unavailable, using unlabelled operational data.

sources.quote: proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data

rationale.text: Her work includes incremental online anomaly detection that maintains performance under concept drift without periodic full retraining.

sources.quote: incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining

rationale.text: She has demonstrated embedded inference feasibility for resource-constrained gateways with quantised and pruned models.

sources.quote: combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: She is open to joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions and prefers applied collaborations that reach real infrastructure.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments.

constraints.text: The detector must work without labelled malicious traffic and cannot rely on supervised classifiers trained on public attack datasets.

sources.quote: we have nothing labelled as malicious

constraints.text: The method must cover both Modbus and BACnet/IP traffic handled by ProtoSense.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic

constraints.text: Alerts must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language.

sources.quote: We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Detection must run on-device on the planned hardware variant without affecting packet forwarding latency.

sources.quote: dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: The collaboration has limited company staffing and data access under NDA.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our traffic archives

constraints.text: Use of the researcher's testbed with industrial partners depends on a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

risks: No BACnet/IP study appears in the supplied researcher material; BACnet detection is a transfer gap from her Modbus/DNP3/PROFINET/EtherNet/IP/OPC UA evidence and must be tested first.

False positives are the company's proven deployment failure mode: a prior supervised classifier caused clients to switch alerts off, so any detector must be calibrated on site-specific normal traffic.
The researcher's availability for a joint project is unknown and could limit scope or timeline.
There are no labelled attacks available from ArmaturaSec clients, so evaluation will depend on controlled or injected scenarios whose representativeness is uncertain.
Plain-language explanation for plant managers is a hard requirement but is not evidenced in the supplied publications.
Budget, timeline and the exact NDA/data-sharing terms are not specified.
questions: What is Prof. Kiss's available time and capacity for this joint project, and does she prefer joint project or industrial PhD supervision?
Does Prof. Kiss have BACnet/IP traffic experience, BACnet captures or BACnet devices for a first transfer experiment?
Which normal traffic archives and hardware bench can ArmaturaSec provide under NDA, and do they include BACnet/IP sites?
What false alarm rate and alert volume do ArmaturaSec clients tolerate, and what explanation format is useful to plant managers?
Can the planned fifth hardware variant run the candidate detector within ProtoSense's latency and memory limits?
What are the project budget, duration, data-sharing agreement and publication/IP terms?
